judgments: The current changing-policy training trajectories show substantial progression regression; the previous clear was real, but used evolving parameters across the run and does not identify one frozen checkpoint.
Early Bomb consumption is the strongest observed difference. Ordinary-or-unconfirmed does not automatically mean every Bomb was unnecessary.
Lower-field occupancy improved as a descriptive training metric, but bottom-edge and side trapping remain. No causal claim follows solely from occupancy.
The new movement-target rewrite is a substantial intervention in addition to small positional reward. It deserves separate evaluation; current data does not isolate its causal effect.

Stored stage4 decisions show stochastic Bomb requests often differ from the frozen family decoder on the same states. This is a credible contributor to train/eval mismatch, not a counterfactual full-game guarantee.
No catastrophic numerical failure or unexecuted updates explains this run. Sample availability in stages5/6 is limited; extending training alone is not an established remedy.

The per-world reset bug consumed18.1% of sampling in unwanted second games and13.3% of PPO rows. A future one-round run must retire completed worlds and handle partial tails instead of resetting to fill batches.
evaluation_plan: Let the existing20-game frozen development evaluation finish with the same opening seeds and decoder as cycle96; compare clears, reach, Miss, Bomb and positions. Keep training paused and do not adjust configurations mid-evaluation.
limits: Different seeds and evolving policies in training; previous16 completed versus current15 completed+1operator stop; stage3/4 event totals include that unfinished first game; alternative geometry is a forecast, not a replayed native outcome.
